guarantees.claim: All outputs are assigned known default values (0 or Inner/SelFifo) at the top of the block; these values take effect whenever a state does not explicitly drive the signal.
In StIdle, update_round is forced to 1 and round_d to Inner every cycle, regardless of the taken branch.
In StIPad, sel_rdata is unconditionally driven to SelIPad; hmac_sha_rvalid is 1 when txcnt_eq_blksz is false and 0 when it is true.
In StMsg, sel_rdata is unconditionally SelFifo and fifo_wsel_o is set to (round_q == Outer).

In StMsg, the state transitions to StWaitResp if ( (Inner && reg_hash_process_flag) || Outer ) && txcount >= sha_message_length_o, or if txcnt_eq_blksz && txcount >= sha_message_length_o && reg_hash_stop_q && Inner. Otherwise it stays in StMsg and drives hmac_sha_rvalid with fifo_rvalid_i.
In StWaitResp, hmac_sha_rvalid is forced to 0. On sha_hash_done_i, the next state becomes StDone if round_q == Outer or (Inner && reg_hash_stop_q), else StPushToMsgFifo.

In StPushToMsgFifo, fifo_wsel_o and fifo_wvalid_o are asserted and clr_fifo_wdata_sel deasserted unconditionally. Transition to StOPad occurs only when fifo_wready_i is true and fifo_wdata_sel_o equals a digest-dependent terminal value (4'd7 for SHA2_256, 4'd15 for SHA2_512, 4'd11 for SHA2_384).
In StOPad, sel_rdata is SelOPad and fifo_wsel_o is 1; hmac_sha_rvalid is 1 unless txcnt_eq_blksz is true, in which case state goes to StMsg with hmac_sha_rvalid=0.
In StDone, hmac_hash_done is pulsed high and the state is forced to StIdle.
The unique case default branch drives st_d to StIdle, providing a safe recovery from any unspecified state encoding.
guarantees.cond: st_q not matching any named state

assumptions.claim: digest_size_i must be one of SHA2_256, SHA2_512, or SHA2_384, because the StPushToMsgFifo transition condition only matches these specific sizes.
assumptions.risk: Any other digest_size_i will cause the state machine to loop forever in StPushToMsgFifo, denying further operation.

assumptions.claim: fifo_wdata_sel_o (driven elsewhere) must be incremented properly and eventually reach 4'd7, 4'd15, or 4'd11 according to the configured digest_size_i.
assumptions.risk: If the counter stalls or mismatches, the state machine will hang in StPushToMsgFifo with fifo_wvalid_o high, potentially overflowing the FIFO or locking up the HMAC core.

assumptions.claim: sha_message_length_o correctly reflects the total message length in the same unit as txcount and is stable during the HMAC operation.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect length may cause premature or late transition out of StMsg, leading to truncated hash or deadlock waiting for counter that never reaches the false length.

assumptions.claim: In StIdle, if both reg_hash_start_i and reg_hash_continue_i are asserted, the RTL gives priority to reg_hash_start_i (start branch). External logic must ensure they are not both active unless that priority is acceptable.
assumptions.risk: If a hardware fault asserts both, the continue operation is ignored and a fresh start occurs, potentially discarding a pre-initialized hash context.

assumptions.claim: txcnt_eq_blksz will eventually become true while the state machine is in StIPad, StOPad, or the second StMsg branch, ensuring progress.
assumptions.cond: state = StIPad, StOPad, or StMsg with stop condition
assumptions.risk: If the block-size counter stalls, the FSM will remain in a wait state indefinitely, stalling the HMAC operation.

assumptions.claim: sha_hash_done_i is a clean pulse that asserts exactly once per hash computation.
assumptions.risk: Multiple assertions or glitches could cause the state machine to advance prematurely or multiple times, corrupting the HMAC sequence.

assumptions.claim: reg_hash_process_flag and reg_hash_stop_q are configured appropriately for the mode; the RTL gives priority to process_flag over stop_q in Inner round when txcount >= sha_message_length_o.
assumptions.cond: Inner round, both flags active, txcount condition met
assumptions.risk: If both flags are set unexpectedly, the FSM will follow the process_flag branch and ignore stop_q, possibly processing extra data or failing to stop at the intended boundary.

uncertain_points.claim: When both reg_hash_process_flag and reg_hash_stop_q are true in Inner round, the first branch in StMsg (line 369-374) takes precedence, skipping the stop condition. It is unclear whether this overlapping configuration is disallowed by the specification.
uncertain_points.cond: st_q == StMsg, round_q == Inner, reg_hash_process_flag and reg_hash_stop_q both 1, txcount >= sha_message_length_o
uncertain_points.risk: The FSM may continue processing beyond the intended stop point, adding unintended data to the hash or altering the key schedule, which could compromise security.

uncertain_points.claim: digest_size_i is used in a comparison that only covers SHA2_256, SHA2_512, and SHA2_384. If any other value (e.g., SHA2_224, or a corrupted value) is present, the transition out of StPushToMsgFifo will never occur.
uncertain_points.cond: st_q == StPushToMsgFifo, digest_size_i not in {SHA2_256, SHA2_512, SHA2_384}
uncertain_points.risk: The HMAC core will hang with fifo_wvalid_o asserted, causing a denial of service and potential write-data corruption if the FIFO back-pressures.
